{
  "needed": true,
  "prompt": "Scope (frontend only): form UX + client-side validation + request payload assembly for the Item create (POST /api/v1/items/) and update (PUT /api/v1/items/{id}) flows. Do not change permission or description rules. Do not assume any backend changes other than the stated behavior (backend stores and returns the processed value).

1) Normalization and validation rules (performed on the client immediately before validation and before submitting):
   - Trim only U+0020 spaces from both ends. Implementation example: use a trim that removes only codepoint U+0020, not other whitespace. Example JS expression: value.replace(/^[\u0020]+|[\u0020]+$/g, '')
   - After trimming, count length by Unicode code points (not UTF-16 code units). In JS use Array.from(trimmed).length or [...trimmed].length so surrogate pairs (e.g., emoji) count as 1.
   - Valid lengths: inclusive between 3 and 80 code points. Anything shorter than 3 or longer than 80 must be rejected client-side before sending.
   - If trimming yields an empty string (original was all U+0020 spaces), treat as invalid.
   - Do not perform any other whitespace normalization or Unicode normalization unless a separate contract exists.

2) Create (POST) behavior on the client:
   - Title is required for create. The client must ensure a title value is present and valid (per rules above) before sending the POST.
   - Before sending, run the U+0020-trim + code point length check. If invalid, block submission and show a validation error.
   - Build POST JSON payload including the processed (trimmed) title string. Never send title: null. Never send title as empty string if invalid.
   - After a successful response, read the title returned by the backend (it is the processed/stored value) and update the UI with that returned value.

3) Update (PUT) behavior on the client:
   - The update endpoint allows omitting title. The client must not change the server value if the user did not modify the title field.
   - Track whether the title input is 'dirty' (user changed it). If the title field was not modified since the form loaded, omit the title property from the PUT JSON entirely.
   - If the user edited the title, apply the same pre-submit normalization & validation (U+0020-trim then code point length check). If invalid, block submission and show validation error.
   - If valid and edited, include title in the PUT payload as the processed (trimmed) string. Never send title: null. If the user cleared the field resulting in an empty trimmed string, treat as invalid and block submission — do not send null to the backend (explicit null is specified to always produce HTTP 422).
   - After a successful response, update the UI with the title returned by the backend.

4) Explicit null handling and omission rule:
   - Do not send title: null from the frontend. The requirement states explicit null will always produce 422; prevent this by client checks.
   - Omit the title property entirely from PUT payloads if the user did not edit the field (this preserves the original server value).

5) Validation UX and timing:
   - Perform trimming+validation at form submit time and also on blur (optional) so users get early feedback. Keep the raw input visible while typing; perform the U+0020-only trimming only when validating or creating the payload (per requirement: strip before submission/validation).
   - Display clear validation messages: e.g. "Title is required" (create), "Title must be 3–80 characters after trimming leading/trailing spaces", "Title cannot be only spaces". If the server returns a 422 with validation details, show the server message; otherwise show the client-side message.

6) Payload construction examples (pseudocode guidance):
   - POST:
     let processed = raw.replace(/^[\u0020]+|[\u0020]+$/g, '');
     if (Array.from(processed).length < 3 || Array.from(processed).length > 80) -> block submit
     body = { title: processed, /* other required fields */ }
   - PUT:
     if (!titleDirty) body = { /* only other fields that changed */ }
     else {
       processed = raw.replace(/^[\u0020]+|[\u0020]+$/g, '')
       if (Array.from(processed).length < 3 || Array.from(processed).length > 80) -> block submit
       body = { title: processed, /* other changed fields */ }
     }
   - Ensure JSON serializer does not include properties with undefined values (omit instead of null).

7) Acceptance test cases to verify on the frontend (must pass/fail as noted):
   - Create with 'ab' (2 code points) -> client validation fail (reject before POST).
   - Create with 'abc' (3 code points) -> client validation pass and POST success.
   - Create with string of exactly 80 code points -> client pass.
   - Create with string of exactly 81 code points -> client fail.
   - Create with leading/trailing U+0020: '␠abc␠' (where ␠ is U+0020) -> trim to 'abc' then validate length.
   - Create with only U+0020 characters ('   ') -> trim to '' -> client validation fail; do not submit.
   - Test with multi-codepoint characters (emoji, surrogate pairs): ensure Array.from(...) counts them as 1. Example: '🙂🙂' counts as 2.
   - Update: open edit form and submit without touching title -> PUT payload must NOT contain title and backend value must remain unchanged.
   - Update: edit title and set a valid new title -> payload includes processed title and backend returns processed title; UI reflects returned title.
   - Update: attempt to send explicit title: null (simulate) -> should not be sent by client; if sent, backend will return 422. Frontend must prevent such payloads.

8) Error handling and server-returned value:
   - If backend returns validation 422 for any reason, display the returned validation errors to the user.
   - After successful create/update, use the title value returned by the backend (do not assume the client-side processed value will be identical — the backend stores/returns the processed value per requirement).

9) Notes and constraints to follow strictly:
   - Only strip U+0020 from ends before validation/submission. Do not remove other Unicode whitespace characters (e.g., NBSP) unless contract changes.
   - Counting must be by Unicode code points. Do not use .length on JS strings (UTF-16 code units) for validation.
   - Do not send title in PUT when the user did not modify it. Do not send title: null in any case.

Deliverables for frontend engineers:
   - Implement client-side U+0020-only trim + code-point length validation on create/update forms per above.
   - Implement dirty-tracking for the title input to decide whether to include title in PUT payloads.
   - Add unit/integration tests covering the acceptance test cases above.
   - Ensure UI shows server-returned title after successful operations.

If any backend contract detail related to how to represent omission vs explicit null for other endpoints is uncertain, stop and request explicit contract before changing behavior. Do not assume alternate behavior beyond what is specified above."
}

**Clarifying frontend requirements**

I need to ensure the frontend doesn't send a null title. If the user clears the title when creating, it should be invalid, but maybe an update can allow that. The requirement states that an explicit null leads to a 422 error, so I should block that from being sent.

For trimming spaces, I only strip leading and trailing U+0020 spaces before validation, measure length by Unicode code points, and reject titles that are too short or long. Also, if the title is all spaces after trimming, it should fail. In updates, we shouldn't include the title in the payload if it hasn't changed, but should include it if the user modifies it.**Drafting frontend implementation instructions**

If the user clears an input, it will end up as an empty string, which should be treated as invalid after trimming. That probably leads to a 422 error if submitted. So, the front-end needs to prevent this submission and display a validation error.

The rules for permissions and descriptions remain unchanged, and I must avoid guessing the server's behavior.

I need to define front-end validation rules and specify how payloads should behave. The focus will be on forms for create and update actions, specifically for POST and PUT endpoints. I'll emphasize Unicode code point counting, suggesting approaches for JavaScript.

For trimming U+0020, I’ll mention using regex or custom methods, guiding developers to avoid trimming other whitespace characters like NBSP.**Clarifying title field handling**

I need to ensure that the title field is sent only when necessary: for creation, I should always include the processed title, while for updates, I’ll send the title only if the user has modified it. I should never send a null title in the payload, even if the UI sets it to null through an API.

If the user clears the title, it should be considered invalid. The front-end should reflect any processed values returned from the server. 

For acceptance tests, I’ll provide test cases covering inputs with leading/trailing spaces, Unicode characters, and surrogate pairs to check code point counting. I’ll include failing tests for lengths of 2 and 81, while ensuring successes for lengths of 3 and 80. Also, when the title remains unchanged in updates, I should omit it entirely and avoid sending nil or explicit null to prevent a server 422 error. Lastly, for creation, if the title is missing, a validation error should be displayed.**Defining validation procedures and feedback**

I need to describe when validation occurs, ideally before submission and on blur for user input. It’s essential to catch client-side errors to prevent invalid payloads from being sent. I should also include handling for error messages and status: if the server returns a 422 error, I’ll show those validation errors in the UI, along with the processed title after a successful response.

I also need instructions for marking a field as "dirty." While I won't make assumptions, I can recommend using plain JavaScript or React libraries. 

The scope focuses on frontend forms for POST and PUT requests, ensuring no server modifications are included. The JSON should return a boolean indicating whether a prompt is necessary, which I've set to true, along with an implementation instructions string. The top-level JSON will contain just those two keys.**Creating implementation instructions**

I’m focused on crafting a clear and step-by-step prompt string in JSON format, avoiding markdown but allowing newlines. The instructions will include precise implementation details.

The normalization step will use a regex to trim spaces. I’ll explain how to count code points in Titles without normalizing whitespace outside of trimming U+0020.

Validation rules will specify required title lengths and conditions for update and create actions. I'll also focus on payload behaviors, error handling for 422 responses, and specific test cases for acceptance conditions.

Implementation notes for React, HTML, or vanilla JS will highlight when to trim and validate. I’ll ensure the final JSON is concise and completes all the requirements without extraneous information.
